methodology: The review discusses the potential applications of thermo-responsive polymers in various fields such as biomedicine, oil&gas, coating, cosmetic industry, concrete industry, paint, and textile. The discussion covers significant areas where these materials have been employed, including cell culture, chromatography, colloidal stabilization, and enhanced oil recovery.
research_objective: To review the great potentialities of thermo-responsive polymers when used to functionalize a target surface or interface in different applications.

key_findings.finding: Polymer materials can change their physico-chemical properties in response to external stimuli such as pH, temperature, light, and redox.
LCST and UCST transitions are entropically driven processes where the phase separation occurs by increasing or decreasing the external temperature, respectively.
Thermo-responsive polymers can be used to modulate the interaction of functionalized surfaces with an external environment, allowing for dynamic behavior.
The cloud point (Tcp) is a parameter that determines the specific application of the polymer and its effectiveness in response to a thermal stimulus.
Thermo-responsive polymers can be used to control cell adhesion and detachment from culture devices.
The incorporation of a solvophobic monomer during the synthesis of LCST-type polymer results in a lower Tcp, while the addition of a solvophilic monomer increases Tcp.
The critical coating thickness affects cell adhesion and proliferation by controlling the LCST and cloud point.
